# Surface and Mesh Extraction
Also called: Gaussian Splatting Mesh Extraction, 3DGS Meshing

## Overview
This family provides methods to extract explicit geometric representations (meshes) or semantic segmentations from trained 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models, which are inherently implicit volumetric representations. It solves the problem of converting these continuous, splatted primitives into discrete, editable, or analyzable structures like triangle meshes or labeled parts. The family is distinguished by its reliance on the opacity and density fields of the Gaussians rather than explicit neural radiance fields or signed distance functions, allowing for direct geometric inference from the splat parameters.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a trained set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives $\mathcal{G} = \{g_1, \dots, g_N\}$. Each primitive $g_i$ is defined by:
*   Center position $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
*   Covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3\times3}$, often parameterized via scaling $S_i$ and rotation $R_i$ such that $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i = R_i S_i S_i^T R_i^T$.
*   Opacity $o_i \in [0, 1]$.
*   View-dependent color represented by spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients $\mathbf{c}_i$.

The core principle is the aggregation of these primitives into a structured field (density, distance, or visibility) that can be processed by standard geometric algorithms (e.g., Marching Cubes, Poisson Reconstruction) or classification algorithms (e.g., Multi-view Voting).

## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md)
A method to extract a 3-D triangulated mesh from a trained Gaussian model without retraining, by building a volumetric density field and extracting an isosurface [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md]. It differs from [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) by relying on opacity-based density accumulation rather than signed distance functions, and from [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md) by operating directly on the 3D primitive structure rather than lifting 2D features.

### [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md)
Distance-based Gaussian Splatting is a method for high-quality rendering and geometric refinement that establishes a structural connection between a large-scale triangle mesh and 3D Gaussian splats [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md]. It solves the problem of redundant or misaligned Gaussian primitives in mesh-based rendering by classifying splats as either "tightly-bound" (close to the mesh surface) or "loosely-bound" (further from the surface) based on a distance threshold [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md]. Unlike sibling methods that may strictly constrain vertices or ignore mesh artifacts, this approach explicitly flattens tightly-bound splats to align with the mesh while allowing loosely-bound splats to capture geometric inaccuracies and details that the mesh alone cannot represent [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md].

### [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md)
This method segments 3D Gaussian primitives in a volume visualization scene by lifting 2D segmentation masks from reference views into 3D space [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md]. It solves the problem of applying distinct editing effects (color, opacity, lighting) to specific parts of a volumetric scene represented by Gaussian splats [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md]. Unlike methods that require learnable feature vectors or complex optimization to define semantic boundaries, this approach is training-free and relies on multi-view label voting to assign labels to primitives [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md]. It is distinct from [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md) and [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) as it targets semantic segmentation for editing rather than geometric mesh extraction [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md].

### Mesh Extraction via Poisson Reconstruction
- [S1, unofficial] Render depth maps from training views using median depth values from splats projected onto pixels.
- [S1, unofficial] Convert the rendered depth maps back into 3D space to derive corresponding normal maps.
- [S1, unofficial] Generate an oriented colored point cloud from the RGB image, depth map, and normal map.
- [S1, unofficial] Input the oriented colored point cloud into the Poisson extraction method to create the textured mesh.

## Background
The extraction of explicit geometry from 3D Gaussian Splatting is a relatively recent development following the introduction of 3DGS [Parent]. Early adaptations, such as AtomGS, utilized depth map rendering and Poisson reconstruction to generate textured meshes from the splatted output [S1, unofficial]. Subsequent works like GOF introduced density-field-based isosurface extraction, while Distance-based Gaussian Splatting integrated mesh constraints directly into the optimization process. These methods address the limitation of 3DGS as a purely visual representation by providing editable, watertight, or semantically labeled geometric outputs.
